Hi Alice — answering each question below (short + concrete):

1) Metadata locality: By default, request metadata (IDs, timestamps, model version, routing metadata) is written to the same region as the inference request. For Redwood-hosted analytics we do aggregate telemetry, but for Enterprise/ Dedicated/Private customers you can opt out of telemetry sharing. For strict in-region guarantee we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment where all logging/analytics endpoints are in your EU tenancy.

2) Cross-region failover: Failover is policy-driven and configurable at the route level. Options: 
   - Strict pinning: fail closed — requests fail if the pinned region is unavailable (recommended for PII-sensitive traffic).
   - Failover allowed: automatic failover to designated sibling region (e.g., US) after N seconds/attempts (configurable).
We can set your PoC routes to "strict pinning" to prevent any cross-region execution unless you authorize a manual intervention.

3) Backups: We support both customer-managed buckets and Redwood-managed buckets. For customer-managed (recommended): nightly snapshots of model artifacts, KV cache, and configuration are written to your S3/GCS buckets in your EU account; we use multipart uploads and server-side encryption with your KMS (you provide the key ARN). Retention is configurable — default 90 days, but we can set custom retention per customer policy. Backups in transit use TLS 1.2+, at-rest uses AES-256 with KMS-managed keys.

4) Logs/audit exports: Yes — audit logs and request logs can be streamed to your SIEM via an in-region forwarder (Kafka/Syslog/HTTPS). We support pushing logs to your Splunk HTTP Event Collector endpoints and can use your KMS for envelope encryption on the log export. Also available: periodic S3 dump of logs if you prefer batch export.

Additional notes: For the PoC we can provision an EU Dedicated cluster and configure route policies and backups as customer-managed. That will give you the strongest in-region guarantees without needing our Private control plane. Pricing implications: dedicated EU cluster is a reserved capacity SKU — Marissa will follow up with a rough estimate.

Let me know if you'd like a short technical runbook or an architecture diagram — I can attach one.

Thanks,
